title: Elevated order-processing latency
alert_or_symptom: Order searches and status updates remain available but are responding much more slowly than normal.

technical_evidence.observation: Order-service p95 response latency increased from 420 milliseconds to 8.6 seconds at 14:05, while the request success rate remained at 99.1 percent.
Transaction database p95 query latency increased from 80 milliseconds to 5.9 seconds; the database remains available.
Slow order traces spend approximately 87 percent of elapsed time waiting for database queries, while application processing time remains within its normal range.
The Application Compute Cluster, Inventory Service and Message Broker are healthy and operating normally.

service_impact.user_impact_description: Approximately 18 percent of order-management requests take between 8 and 12 seconds, but requests generally complete successfully.
service_impact.workaround_description: Users can retry delayed order searches; requests generally complete on retry.

environmental_context: The Order Management Service depends on the Transaction Database Cluster.

recent_changes.description: A routine database statistics refresh completed at 13:50.

reported_unknowns: The specific database query, lock or resource condition associated with the increased latency has not been identified.
The expected duration of the degradation is not yet known.
additional_context: No failed orders, duplicate orders, data loss or security exposure have been observed.
